newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SCOTLAND HIT BY INJURIES AHEAD OF TRIP TO BALTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCOTLAND HIT BY INJURIES AHEAD OF TRIP TO BALTICS.

text.p: Three of Scotland's top players were ruled out by injury on Wednesday from the squad heading for the Baltic states this week for two vital World Cup qualifiers.
Blackburn defender Colin Hendry and Glasgow Rangers strikers Ally McCoist and Gordon Durie will all miss the clashes with Latvia on Saturday and Estonia next Wednesday.
Everton forward Duncan Ferguson had already ruled out because of an operation and several other players are doubtful.
"Colin Hendry phoned me yesterday to alert me there may be a problem and unfortunately he has had to call off," manager Craig Brown said.
"He will have a hernia operation tomorrow and now my main hope is that Colin will be back playing for Blackburn against Liverpool the week before we meet Sweden on November 10.
"Gordon Durie and Ally McCoist are also not fit -- we were advised of this by the Rangers doctor today -- so we have a few problems.
"You can add the likes of Ferguson, Paul McStay, Alan McLaren and even Craig Levein who we have also had to do without."
Blackburn forward Kevin Gallacher remains a fitness doubt and Brown said he may call up English first division players Doug Freedman of Crystal Palace and John McGinlay of Bolton.
"These guys have club games at the weekend so I want to be absolutely fair to them before I call them in," Brown said. "I'd have to be sure they were going to be on the bench at least.
"The call-offs are undoubtedly a blow, but I'm still cautiously optimistic that we can win both games. However, we'll have to be at our very best to collect six points."
